diagnostic_evidence.quote: U_{n} = e^{n\tau A}U_0 + \tau \sum_{k=0}^{n} c_k e^{(n-k)\tau A}G(\Pi_{\tau^{-1}}U_{k}).

issues.failure_explanation: As defined, W_n contains the sum over k without the step-size factor tau, while the right-hand side uses the ell^1_tau norm, which carries a factor tau. Applying the homogeneous discrete Strichartz estimate termwise yields a bound by sum_k ||F_k||_{L^2} = tau^{-1} ||F||_{ell^1_tau L^2}, not by ||F||_{ell^1_tau L^2}. Counterexample: f=g=0, F_0=h, other F_k=0; then W_n = e^{n tau A}(0,h) has ell^p_tau L^q norm comparable to ||h||_{L^2} (frequency-localized Sobolev), whereas the claimed bound is tau||h||_{L^2}, which tends to 0. The proof ('treated in the same manner') does not supply the missing factor.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the factor tau in front of the sum in the definition of W_n (matching the discrete Duhamel formula), or equivalently replace ||F||_{ell^1_{tau,T}L^2} by sum_k ||F_k||_{L^2} in the bound.
issues.overall_effect: The corollary as stated is false. Its only use is in Lemma LemDiskrWellp via the discrete Duhamel formula (DiskrDuhamelStrang), which does contain tau in front of the sum, so the intended (corrected) version is what is actually used; downstream results remain valid once the statement is corrected.
issues.title: Discrete inhomogeneous Strichartz corollary misstated: sum lacks factor tau, so the bound in terms of the ell^1_tau norm is false
issues.why_classification: A local, routine correction of the statement restores a true result and all applications already use the corrected form; no argument or guarantee is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \mathrm{Err}_m \le c\|E_{N_m}\|_{H^1 \times L^2} + c\tau^\frac12 + cT_1^{\frac12}\mathrm{Err}_m \le c\mathrm{Err}_{m-1} + c\tau^\frac12 + \frac12 \mathrm{Err}_m.
Let $c=c(M,T)$ be the maximum of $1$ and the implicit constants from \eqref{eq:Rekalpha4H1} and \eqref{eq:Rekalpha4L2}.

issues.failure_explanation: With T_1 <= c^{-2} one only obtains cT_1^{1/2} <= 1, so the displayed inequality cT_1^{1/2} Err_m <= (1/2) Err_m is not justified; the term c T_1^{1/2} Err_m cannot be absorbed into the left-hand side as written, and the recursion Err_m <= 2c(Err_{m-1} + tau^{1/2}) does not follow from the stated choice of T_1. The same gap affects the analogous L^2 x H^{-1} recursion.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose T_1 := min{T, b_0, (2c)^{-2}} (so that cT_1^{1/2} <= 1/2); the rest of the proof, including L = ceil(2T/T_1) and the constants C and tau_0, goes through unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The iterative argument establishing the alpha=4 error bounds of Theorem ThmStrang (and, by the same construction, the alpha=4 part of Theorem ThmStrangFully) has a gap in the absorption step as written; no conclusion is lost once the constant is adjusted.
issues.title: Absorption step in the alpha=4 global error proof fails with the chosen T_1 (cT_1^{1/2} <= 1, not <= 1/2)
issues.why_classification: A one-line change of a constant in the definition of T_1 repairs the inference with no change to method, rates, or scope.
